reason: The passage demonstrates Yahweh actively protecting and blessing the Hebrew people (Bnei Yisrael) through multiple explicit interventions. When Balak hires Balaam to curse Israel, Yahweh refuses ('לֹא תָאֹר אֶת־ הָעָם כִּי בָרוּךְ הוּא' - you shall not curse them, for they are blessed) and forcibly directs Balaam to bless Israel instead, even against Balaam's initial instructions. The text explicitly states 'יְהוָה אֱלֹהָיו עִמּוֹ' (Yahweh their God is with them) and references Yahweh's past deliverance: 'אֵל מוֹצִיאָם מִמִּצְרַיִם' (God brought them out of Egypt). The blessings pronounced over Israel celebrate their strength, prosperity, and favor—all portrayed as divine gifts. The entire narrative structure shows Yahweh intervening decisively to ensure Israel's protection and success, which unmistakably demonstrates that supporting the Hebrew people is a central divine purpose.
